clue.text: Even tailless bird cuts bottom

indicators.note: a piece that cuts another is driven into its middle, so the bird sits inside the bottom

parts.note: rear means the bottom or backside

indicators.note: a bird with no tail loses its final letter

parts.note: a gull is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird missing its tail feathers somehow levels off or wounds someone's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Even' looks like an adverb but is the adjective meaning steady; 'bottom' is the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something regular is even, steady and uniform in pattern.

clue.text: Summarises about headwear

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
caps are items of headwear

explanation.surface: Someone gives a brief account of hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recap is to sum up the main points briefly.

clue.text: Good bananas, thick and gooey

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, as is loopy

explanation.surface: Fine bananas, mashed to a dense sticky mush.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something gloopy is viscous and sticky, like thick sauce.

clue.text: Awful illness overshadowing one's solitude

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the letters of illness and one are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A terrible illness casts a shadow over someone's lonely life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges ILLNESS and ONE together; the 's is is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: solitude is the state of being alone, which brings isolation.

clue.text: Direct attention up and down

definitions.note: to direct someone's attention to a source is to point them to it; the word reads the same both ways

indicators.note: the word reads the same going up the down light as coming down it

parts.note: to direct someone's attention to a source is to point them to it; the word reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: An instruction to look upwards and then downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to refer someone to something is to direct their attention towards it.

clue.text: Fetches vehicle and trailer's oddly missing

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the even letters of the word trailer's remain

explanation.surface: Someone collects a car but finds the trailer has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly missing' drops T, A, L and E from TRAILER'S, leaving RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fetch something is to carry it from one place to another.

clue.text: Make prisoner cold with stiff walk outside

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: the walk goes outside the cold, wrapping round it

parts.note: to strut is to walk stiffly and proudly

explanation.surface: An inmate is forced out into the cold for a rigid march in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts STRUT round C, giving STRUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to construct something is to make or build it.

clue.text: Laugh hysterically from paddle on river? On the contrary

indicators.note: the reverse of the stated order: the river goes on top of the paddle, not the paddle on the river

parts.note: an oar is a paddle for rowing

explanation.surface: Someone bursts out laughing at a rower on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means above; 'On the contrary' flips it, so R comes above OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to roar with laughter is to laugh loudly and helplessly.

clue.text: Bury stick, leaving evidence finally for detectives

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: leaving means a letter departs from the stick

parts.note: a pole is a long stick

indicators.note: finally says only the last letter of the word evidence is used

explanation.surface: Someone hides a stick, leaving clues behind for investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' with 'evidence finally' takes E off POLE to give POL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Interpol is the international organisation of police forces that coordinates detective work.

clue.text: Bug sleek and smooth without large head

indicators.note: without means the large letter is removed

parts.note: slick means sleek and smooth
a ness is a headland, a head projecting into the sea

explanation.surface: Describing an insect that is shiny, smooth and without a big head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes L out of SLICK, giving SICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bug is an informal word for an illness or infection.

clue.text: Show off new top

parts.note: to crow is to boast or show off

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a brand-new shirt or blouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the crown is the top of the head or of a hill.

clue.text: Exotic wild cat faints

indicators.note: wild suggests letters running out of control, so the words cat faints are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exotic wild cat keels over in a faint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something fantastic is strange and fanciful, far from the everyday.

clue.text: Dad performing ritual with yen for acclaim

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a father

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of the word ritual being acted out in a new order

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A father carrying out a ritual, eager for applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: popularity is widespread approval, the state of being acclaimed by many.

clue.text: Allow no time for relation

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is not wanted and is struck out

parts.note: to grant is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to give a relative any of their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a grandmother is a family relation, and this is her informal name.

clue.text: Possible result of fare reduction?

parts.note: fare looks like a ticket price, but here it is food; cutting food intake far enough leads to hunger

explanation.surface: What might happen if transport ticket prices were lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' reads as a ticket price, but it is food, so reducing it means eating less.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: fare also means food, and cutting food to nothing leads to deadly hunger.

clue.text: Orders in street ahead of disturbances

indicators.note: one piece placed ahead of another comes first in the answer

parts.note: ructions are noisy disturbances or rows

explanation.surface: Commands given in the street just before riots break out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: instructions are orders or directions to be carried out.

clue.text: Rant with idiot — bad habit

indicators.note: bad suggests the words rant and idiot are spoiled and reassembled

explanation.surface: Ranting along with a fool is a bad habit to get into.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tradition is a custom or long-established habit.

clue.text: Guess I'm stuck in large property

indicators.note: the words I'm are stuck in the property, placed inside it

parts.note: an estate is a large area of land and property

explanation.surface: Someone guesses they are trapped inside a big country house.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an estimate is a rough calculation or guess.

clue.text: Tries cast every now and then with lures

indicators.note: every now and then picks letters at regular gaps, the second and fourth of the word cast

parts.note: to tempt is to lure

explanation.surface: An angler casts occasionally using lures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every now and then' takes A and T from CAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: attempts are tries or efforts.

clue.text: Planted oneself? Is plant okay?

parts.note: to sit down is to plant oneself, so planted oneself is sat
a plant is an industrial works or factory

explanation.surface: Someone who has sat down asks whether a houseplant is doing fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' is the industrial sense, not the green one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something satisfactory is acceptable, good enough, all right.

clue.text: Bird we picked up following wind

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: to wind, as with hair, is to curl

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted so the word we reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: We spot a bird after a gust of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' sounds like a homophone signal, but in a down light it turns WE into EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the curlew is a wading bird with a long down-curved bill.

clue.text: Some may do lemonade — if upset, that sounds good

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the run reads from bottom to top
some of the words are taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A spilled lemonade might be fine, according to some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks YDOLEM from 'may do lemonade', and 'upset' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a melody is a tune, a pleasing sequence of musical notes.

clue.text: Thought that is keeping daughter awake, initially

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: IE (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of the word awake is used

explanation.surface: A worry that is keeping a daughter awake at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts D inside IE to give IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an idea is a thought or notion in the mind.

clue.text: Books torn — rue it later

indicators.note: torn suggests the words rue it later being ripped apart and put together differently

explanation.surface: Tearing up books is something you may regret afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: literature is written works collectively, books in general.

clue.text: Keen, for example, to secure article on the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the earlier letters sit on top of the queen
to secure something is to hold it fast inside

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An example of someone enthusiastic to obtain an item about the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts A inside EG, giving EAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be eager is to be keen and enthusiastic.

clue.text: End story for the listener

indicators.note: for the listener means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Finishing a story read out to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the tail is the end or rear part of something.

clue.text: A ringing sound including another is attractive

indicators.note: one sound including another holds it inside

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing sound
another ringing sound is a peal of bells

explanation.surface: A ringing sound that includes another sound is pleasing to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: Two different ringing sounds are needed: the short one wraps around the bell-tower one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something appealing is attractive and pleasing.

clue.text: US soldier repelled by John's icy house

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the soldier's letters run backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
john is slang for a toilet, as is loo; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: An American soldier is turned away from John's frosty home.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an igloo is an Inuit dome built from blocks of snow and ice.

clue.text: Greek character records one learner working

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
I is the Roman numeral one
L is the learner driver's plate
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A Greek eccentric records a lone student at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Be in charge of a strategy to beat it

parts.note: to run something is to be in charge of it
a way of doing something is a method or strategy

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lead a plan for winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it' is slang for leave quickly, not defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to beat it is slang for fleeing, leaving in a hurry.
